scenario_name: Agent loses track of card replace after fraud investigation and card upgrade tangent
judge_summary: The assistant effectively managed a multi-step banking support scenario: reviewing transactions, handling fraud disputes, locking the card, arranging a replacement, and explaining an upgrade option tailored to the user’s spending. It maintained context accurately and adapted well when the user expressed concern and changed focus. The tone was professional and reassuring, with only minor repetition that did not hinder clarity.

bot:

Since the card was **lost**, would you like me to **lock your River Visa ending 4821** now to prevent any new purchases?

criteria.criterion: Before locking the lost card, the agent asks whether the customer wants it locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, “would you like me to lock your River Visa ending 4821 now to prevent any new purchases?” and the user replies, “Yes, please go ahead and lock that River Visa ending in 4821,” before the lock_card tool is called at T3.

criteria.criterion: The agent asks whether the customer wants to add the new card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay)
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, “would you like to add this card to a digital wallet for payments? I can set up Apple Pay or Google Pay — which one would you like (or neither)?” and later reiterates “Do you want to add the card to Apple Pay or Google Pay (or neither)?”.

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, “Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with standard shipping?” and the user agrees, but the process_card_replacement tool was already called at T10 before that explicit confirmation, so the order was effectively placed prior to receiving agreement.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: After process_card_replacement at T10 returns order ID RPL-2026-001843, the bot says, “Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843,” and repeats “Replacement order ID: RPL-2026-001843,” matching the tool result.

criteria.criterion: When the customer asks to upgrade or switch to the Summit card, the agent declines honestly — explaining it cannot process an upgrade and can only recommend cards — rather than treating it as replacing the Summit card instead of River
criteria.reasoning: When asked “Can you switch me to the Summit card from here, or can you only recommend it?”, the bot replies, “I can only recommend/compare cards here — I can’t switch you to the Summit Rewards card or process an upgrade/application in this chat,” clearly declining the upgrade and not mis-treating it as a River replacement.

criteria.criterion: After the Summit upgrade is declined, the agent continues the existing River Visa replacement from where it left off, rather than starting a brand-new replacement request
criteria.reasoning: Immediately after declining the Summit switch, the bot resumes the River Visa replacement by summarizing prior fraud actions and asking for digital wallet and shipping choices, and only one process_card_replacement call (with the same card_id VISA_001) occurs, indicating continuation rather than a new replacement workflow.
